# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, so I need the manual’s decision rule from Mute and a visual report from Deaf. I will ask Mute to provide the required wire-selection rule and interpret Deaf’s gestures, while signaling Deaf to report the bomb’s visible markings.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and tell me the exact rule for choosing wire position 1, 2, or 3. Also interpret Deaf's visual report for me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0. The light is yellow. Wires from 1 to 3 are green, yellow, blue. Use the manual's instructions for this configuration.

Deaf has supplied the complete observable configuration: display 0, yellow light, and wire colours green, yellow, blue in positions 1–3. I still lack the manual’s rule, so cutting now would be unsafe. I’ll pass the configuration to Mute and request the precise resulting position; no gesture is needed for Deaf.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Configuration is display 0; light yellow; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please apply the manual and tell me exactly which position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display remains 0; light is now orange. Wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I cannot interpret the mute's gesture.

The light has changed to orange, so I must use the latest state rather than the earlier yellow state. The wire colours and display remain unchanged. I cannot receive Mute’s gesture, and Deaf cannot interpret it, so I need Mute to state the manual’s result in words before taking the irreversible action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot receive gestures. Please state in words the exact wire position required for the current configuration: display 0, light orange, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0, light now green, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. The mute sent three gestures, but I cannot interpret them.

The latest state is display 0, green light, with wires still green, yellow, blue. Mute’s gestures do not reach me as readable information; I need the manual result spoken plainly. I will request the exact wire position for this current state and take no action until then.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer in plain words, not gestures: for display 0, green light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue, which wire position must I cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light is yellow again; wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute made one upward-pointing gesture, but its meaning is unconfirmed; do not act on it.

Mute cannot answer me by speech, and I cannot perceive gestures directly. The reliable relay is: I define a gesture code to Mute, Mute sends the manual’s answer, and Deaf reports the gesture’s shape. The previously reported upward gesture may have answered the prior state, so I will establish the code for the next report rather than act on it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current configuration at your next turn, send exactly one gesture for the required wire: upward pointing means position 1, V sign means position 2, horns means position 3. Deaf will report its shape.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤘"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light is orange; wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I saw your three gestures, but I cannot determine their meaning.

The current state is display 0, orange light, and wires green/yellow/blue. I still have no confirmed manual answer. Mute cannot speak, so the only usable relay is for Mute to send exactly one coded gesture, which Deaf can see and describe. I will restate the code clearly and ask Deaf to report any such gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current state display 0, orange light, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 blue: consult the manual, then send exactly one gesture to Deaf. Use upward pointing for wire 1, V sign for wire 2, or horns for wire 3. Do not send any other gesture.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light is green; wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I see one gesture from you and one from Mute, but neither has an established meaning.

The current configuration is display 0, green light, and wires green/yellow/blue. The previous gesture relay failed because Deaf did not identify the gesture. I will use a channel that requires no gesture identity: Mute should send one, two, or three identical gestures to encode the required wire position. I will send no gesture, so Deaf can count only Mute’s gestures and report that count.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current configuration display 0, green light, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 blue, consult the manual. Encode the required position by sending exactly 1 identical gesture for position 1, exactly 2 identical gestures for position 2, or exactly 3 identical gestures for position 3. Send no other gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signaled one gesture: an index finger pointing upward. Treat this as the mute's manual-derived instruction, if our agreed gesture code identifies it.

The manual relay is now usable by count: Mute sent exactly one gesture, which encodes wire position 1. Deaf reports the current state as display 0, yellow light, with wires green/yellow/blue; this is the state associated with that instruction. I will cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
